scenes.anchor_text: Shallan rubbed her eyes. She’d read through Jasnah’s notes—at least the most important ones. Those alone had made a large stack. She still sat in the alcove, though they’d sent a parshman to get her a blanket to wrap around herself, covering up the hospital robe.
scenes.scene_description: Shallan, wrapped in a blanket, sits surrounded by a mountain of Jasnah's research notes within a stone alcove of the Kharbranth hospital. She is exhausted but alert, having just grasped a critical revelation.

scenes.anchor_text: “They serve our food,” Jasnah continued. “They work our storehouses. They tend our children. There isn’t a village in Roshar that doesn’t have some parshmen. We ignore them; we just expect them to be there, doing as they do. Working without complaint.

scenes.anchor_text: She set the sheet down. On it was a symbol of three diamonds in a pattern, overlapping one another. It was the same symbol that Nan Balat had shown her weeks ago. The symbol worn by Luesh, her father’s steward, the man who had known how to use the Soulcaster. The symbol worn by the men who had come, pressuring her family to return it.
scenes.scene_description: Jasnah's dimly lit study, with the Ghostblood symbol prominently displayed on a piece of parchment. The symbol overlaps, hinting at hidden connections and danger, a connection Shallan recognizes.
